Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G2041; inactive, i.e. unemployed; (by implication) lazy, useless:--barren, idle, slow.
BiblicalUsage: The word means idle, inactive, unemployed, and by extension useless or lazy. Jesus says men will give account for every idle word, the householder finds men standing idle in the marketplace, James says faith without works is dead, and Paul quotes the Cretans as lazy gluttons.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that idleness is not rest, it is a refusal to work, and the Bible treats it as a sin with an account to give. Faith that does nothing is dead, and words that do nothing will be answered for.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; James, Brother of Jesus; Paul; Titus
